summary: M0 model-only verdict: BENIGN @ 0.78. All 130 sign-in events for g.sen@aegean.edu come from one known device (dev-gs-phone) in Manisa, TR, alternating only between the user's home ISP (198.51.100.140, Superonline) and the university network (193.140.10.62, AS-AEGEAN-EDU). There is no impossible travel, no new device, no new ASN/country/city, no MFA bypass or fatigue, and no auth from the phishing infrastructure. The two mail events show a phishing email (edevlet-burs-basvuru.com, KYK scholarship lure) that was delivered and clicked (/giris), but there is no follow-on sign-in activity indicating account takeover. The suspicious phish-click signal is explained by the absence of any compromise indicators across the full authentication history.
limitations: M0 ablation: Nemotron alone, no tools, no Critic, no Risk Gate, no DQ. Not a product configuration.
